Poulet Nan Sos (Haitian Chicken in Sauce)

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 50 min

Poulet Nan Sos, or Chicken in Sauce, is a beloved and iconic Haitian dish, often served at celebrations and family gatherings. For the Fête de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, this hearty and flavorful chicken stew symbolizes the bounty of the land and the simple, nourishing meals associated with the agricultural spirit of Papa Zaka, the Lwa of farmers and the harvest.

Ingredients

  • 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts)
  • 2-3 limes, juiced (or 1/4 cup / 60 ml white vinegar)
  • 1 large green bell pepper, roughly chopped
  • 1 medium yellow onion, roughly chopped
  • 6-8 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) fresh parsley, roughly chopped
  • 2-3 sprigs fresh thyme (leaves only, or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 Scotch bonnet pepper (optional, for heat, seeds removed if less heat desired)
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) olive oil or vegetable oil
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) tomato paste
  • 1 large tomato, diced (or 1/2 cup / 120 ml canned diced tomatoes)
  • 2 cups (480 ml) hot water or chicken broth
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste

Method

  1. Clean the chicken: Place chicken pieces in a large bowl, add the juice of 2 limes (or vinegar) and enough water to cover. Rub the chicken thoroughly, then rinse well under cold water. Pat dry with paper towels.
  2. Prepare the epis (Haitian seasoning blend): In a food processor or blender, combine the green bell pepper, half of the onion, garlic, parsley, thyme, and the Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Blend until a smooth paste forms. This is your epis.
  3. Marinate the chicken: In a large bowl, combine the cleaned chicken pieces with about half of the prepared epis. Mix well to coat every piece. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.
  4. Brown the chicken: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in batches, without overcrowding the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides, about 3-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
  5. Sauté aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining half of the chopped onion and the remaining epis to the pot. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until fragrant and softened.
  6. Build the sauce: Stir in the tomato paste and diced fresh tomato (or canned tomatoes). Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the tomato paste to deepen in color.
  7. Simmer the stew: Return the browned chicken pieces to the pot. Pour in the hot water or chicken broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30-40 minutes, or until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
  8. Adjust seasoning and serve: Taste the sauce and adjust salt and pepper if needed. Serve hot with white rice, plantains, or bread to soak up the delicious sauce.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, make the epis a day ahead and let it marinate with the chicken overnight.
  • Add root vegetables like diced potatoes or carrots during the last 20 minutes of cooking for a heartier stew.
  • If you prefer less heat, omit the Scotch bonnet pepper entirely or use just a small piece without the seeds.
